title: Lightning Can Shoot Upward Into Space Like Red Jellyfish

scenes.text: Red lightning shoots upward from storms, fifty miles high.
They are called sprites, and they flash above the clouds.
They glow red because of nitrogen in the air.
Each one lasts only a few milliseconds, far too fast to notice.
They were discovered by accident in 1989, when a physicist was testing a low-light camera on a clear night.
Lightning goes down. Sometimes it goes up too. Now watch it again.

description:
Red sprites are flashes of light that shoot upward from thunderstorms to about 50 miles high.
They last only milliseconds and were discovered by accident in 1989.
Have you ever seen one?
first_comment: Bonus: astronauts on the space station have photographed sprites from above. Would you chase storms to see one?
